subject: Sustained throughput evaluation & MAP: FinVault trial (TTFT, tokens/sec, econ)

Subject: MAP & perf numbers we need to sign

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Finance and infra are aligned; procurement asked for a mutual action plan that includes concrete throughput numbers we can rely on for pricing. Specifically we need:

- Sustained QPS target (for our 2k concurrent users expected peak) and tokens/sec estimates
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) at cold/warm start and steady state
- Concurrency guidelines (per-GPU and per-pod) you validated in tests
- Unit economics: $/1M tokens and approximate $/sustained-QPS-hour at target config

Can you send a draft MAP with planned evaluation steps, the test environments you will run, and expected sign-off dates? Procurement would like to push toward a purchase order by end of month if numbers check out.

Best,
Dana

Hi Dana — thanks for the clear list. Attached is a draft MAP spreadsheet (FinVault_MAP_Throughput_Plan.xlsx) and I summarized the key evaluation items below. Ben and Lauren are on the thread to run the tests and model the unit economics. Proposed timeline:

- Week 1 (Aug 24-28): discovery + dataset and prompt-set freeze
- Week 2 (Aug 31-Sep 4): controlled run: sustained-throughput test (multi-hour) + TTFT matrix
- Week 3 (Sep 7-11): results analysis, cost modeling, executive review
- Contract/PO target: Sep 15

Test environment (short):
- Model family: redwood-llama-70b-quant-v2 (customer-visible name in catalog)
- Hardware: Dedicated A100-80GB pools (pinned for test), 4 pods, autoscaling off for controlled run
- Typical prompt: 120 tokens input, 350 token generation average (prompt set attached)
- Measurement windows: 15m warmup, 3h sustained window, per-request latency traces captured

Deliverables: MAP spreadsheet, throughput results PDF, TTFT/quantiles, econ sheet with $/1M tokens and $/QPS-hr.

Let us know if procurement needs specific formatting for the numbers for the PO.

- Olga

Dana / Olga — looping in the runbook details. Quick notes from our lab pre-checks:

- Baseline config used for sustained run: batch_size=16, kv_cache_prefetch=on, per-pod concurrency cap=48 (to avoid OOM at peak seq len)
- Warm cache TTFT (median): ~36ms; cold-start median TTFT: ~210ms on A100 pool (single request path, no warm workers)
- Sustained tokens/sec observed in dry runs (350-gen average) at 3 pods pinned: ~95k tokens/sec aggregate (~31.6k tokens/sec per pod)
- Sustained QPS (350-token outputs) translates to ~270 QPS aggregate (3 pods), sustained for 1 hour in dry run without errors

Economics sketch (preliminary):
- Direct infra burn (A100 pooled): $2.20 / pod-hour at our dedicated pricing layer
- Effective cost per 1M tokens (at observed sustained throughput, including infra amortized + ops): ~$18 - $24 / 1M tokens depending on cache hit-rate assumptions
- Cost per sustained-QPS-hour (e.g., 100 sustained QPS): ~$7.5 - $10 depending on pod utilization and batching efficiency

I will run the controlled 3-hour sustained test and attach the formal results PDF.

-Ben

Thanks Ben — these numbers look promising. A couple of follow-ups before we sign: 

1) Can you provide P95 and P99 TTFT under sustained load? Procurement wants to see tail behavior for SLA drafting.
2) For our billing model we need a simple $/1M tokens and a per-month committed price for 500 QPS sustained baseline. Can you produce both committed and on-demand econ rows?
3) Any recommended concurrency cap per pod when we enable autoscaling?

If you can get the P95/P99 and the committed pricing row by Aug 30 we can escalate to procurement and legal.

-Dana
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP & perf numbers we need to sign

Dana — ran the extended 3-hour controlled run and calculated the tails and econ rows you asked for. Highlights pasted below; full traces are in the attached PDF and the MAP spreadsheet has the committed pricing row.

Observations (3-hour sustained window, 4 pods pinned for final run):
- Aggregate sustained tokens/sec: 132k tokens/sec (4 pods) => ~33k tokens/sec per pod
- Sustained QPS (avg for 350-token outputs): ~377 QPS aggregate
- Median TTFT (warm): 34ms; P95 TTFT (warm): 120ms; P99 TTFT (warm): 210ms
- Cold-start median TTFT seen in cold-worker injection tests: 220ms; cold P95: 480ms
- Error rate during sustained run: 0.03% (retries handled by client), no OOMs observed

Unit economics (finalized rows):
- On-demand: $/1M tokens = $22.50 (includes infra + ops + small margin)
- Committed (12-month, reserved capacity for 4 pods baseline at 500 QPS sustained): $/1M tokens = $14.75
- Committed monthly fee (500 QPS sustained baseline): $34,500 / month (includes reserved pods and 24/7 support SLA)
- Cost per sustained-QPS-hour (at committed pricing): ~$6.10/QPS-hour equivalent when amortized across tokens and reserved capacity

Autoscaling recommendation:
- Concurrency cap per pod: 48 for safety, increase to 64 only if you enable aggressive KV prefetch and have sequence-length distribution capped at 450 tokens; recommended target pod size: 4-6 pods for 500 QPS with burst headroom

Next steps: I will update the MAP sheet to include the P95/P99 lines and the committed pricing table. Olga — happy to have your procurement contact pick a time next week to review the PO language.

-ben
